name: IL-09
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by about 19 points, anchoring the seat to the party holding it
Daniel Biss has raised nearly $3 million while John Elleson shows minimal reported fundraising
Open seat after Jan Schakowsky's retirement removes incumbency but not the district's partisan character
Prediction markets price a Democratic win around 95 percent
model.rationale: The 9th District's strong Democratic lean plus Biss's decisive financial advantage over an underfunded Republican opponent keep this seat safely Democratic despite the open seat. Outside spending against Biss is notable but unlikely to overcome a ~19-point partisan baseline.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending against Biss combined with an unusually favorable national Republican environment could narrow the margin enough to matter.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Jan Schakowsky (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Illinois's 9th District is a heavily Democratic seat covering the Chicago north suburbs and lakefront, and longtime incumbent Jan Schakowsky's retirement does not change its fundamental partisan character. Daniel Biss enters the general election as the clear Democratic favorite, having raised nearly $3 million for the race. Republican John Elleson has reported little in fundraising or cash on hand, leaving a large resource gap.

Outside groups have spent against Biss, but expenditures at this scale have rarely been enough to overcome a district that has favored Democrats by roughly 19 points. Prediction markets price a Democratic win at about 95 percent. With no public general-election polling available, the forecast rests on district fundamentals, which point to a comfortable Democratic hold in the low twenties.
